benchmark.scope: Runner's measured formal workload, excluding warmup under the cube-bench contract. Includes scheduling and result collection; create-delete mode also includes deletion. Generic producers must use this same scope.

command.scope: Collector's external-command wall-clock window; may include warmup, setup, cleanup and console draining. Not the formal benchmark duration.

capture.scope: Collector's entire wall-clock capture window, including surrounding log/metrics collection. Not the formal benchmark duration.

warmup.definition: Warmup is a configured number of serial benchOne iterations before formal timing. It uses the selected mode: create-only creates sandboxes; create-delete also deletes them. The HTTP client is reused by the formal workload.
warmup.runner_scope: Official cube-bench excludes warmup from summary.total_time_s and exported raw samples; generic producers must document the same boundary. A configured count is not proof that warmup succeeded.
warmup.component_scope: Server logs may contain both warmup and formal instances. Without an explicit ID-to-phase mapping, retain unknown_phase; never remove the first N log records or infer phase from timestamp order.

warnings: Command/capture timestamps use collector wall time and can be affected by clock adjustments; they are not monotonic runner timing.
cubemastercli_instance_ids_collected: 100 formal run IDs available under declared template exclusivity and validated cube-bench warmup=0
client_sample_id_mapping_unavailable: CLI inventory does not map client seq to server IDs

limitations: Whole-run duration measures concurrent workload completion, not a sum or maximum of individual request latencies.
Timing fields and generic clock declarations are producer-supplied evidence; they do not independently certify workload execution or success.
Request counts describe supplied raw rows; missing raw input remains unknown even when a summary reports totals.
create_latency_ms is the existing profile.benchmark.create distribution of valid successful samples, not whole-run timing.
